inputPlan.scheduleMode: original wall-time schedule; no state polling drives input
inputPlan.resetForDiagnosis: existing resetGame() called after optional ready screenshot; diagnostic only

startupAlignment.note: Before reset, browser startup simulation progress was not identical. This is a confounder in the original comparison. The paired runs reset to the same default seed/level/ready/progress before the schedule.

observationBoundary.primary: window capture listener records state before the native shell pointerdown handler; window bubble listener records state after the handler returns, before a later frame snapshot.
observationBoundary.inputDisposition: All first-four inputs produced an immediate launch/flip transition at the handler boundary. No buffered-only or ignored input was observed in this paired window; inputBuffer is not asserted when no visible transition occurs.

withScreenshotsFirst.afterInput: Both native handlers immediately emitted flip at their own pointerdown boundary.

withoutScreenshotsFirst.afterInput: Both native handlers immediately emitted flip at the same physical step; only the pre-input pose/velocity differed.

minimalReverification.result: The stable explanation is scheduling/path history before input 4: screenshot capture changes the elapsed wall-time between inputs, so inputs land in different physical steps and the pre-input pose diverges. In the swapped run, input 4 lands in the same physical step and still has different pre-input pose, while the pointerdown handler emits the same immediate flip. This rules out a screenshot-specific input-handler semantic change at input 4, but does not claim screenshot overhead is harmless; it remains the cause of timing/path divergence in these runs.
minimalReverification.remainingBoundary: The exact RAF-to-native-pointer dispatch latency is recorded only at the browser receipt boundary; no source hook exposes the private ActionInput accepted/buffered flag. A no-transition input would therefore remain classified as buffered-or-ignored unless a later event can be causally matched.
